verdict.reasoning: Patient reports pins and needles in right hand with perceived arm weakness and leg weakness plus gait change: “pins and needles in the hand… my arm is getting weaker… my colleague said, I'm walking slightly differently… at the same time I get my arm symptoms, my leg feels weaker.”
Onset and changing frequency stated: “probably a month and a half, maybe two months” and “at the start, it would be maybe once a week… once a month, but now it's… a couple of times a day.”
Duration and current status described: “it only lasts few days and then goes back to normal” and later “Do you have the symptoms right now? Patient: No, I'm perfectly fine at the moment.”

During episodes: “pins and needles… in the hand… my arm is getting weaker… at the same time I get my arm symptoms, my leg feels weaker” and colleague noted gait change: “my colleague said, I'm walking slightly differently to normal.”

New symptoms and timing: “recently I've noticed, I can't hold my cup of coffee… when I do drink coffee, it's slightly harder to drink… that's only been in the last couple of days… only during the episodes” and throat sensation: “I feel like there's something in my throat.”
No dysarthria or visual symptoms: “What about… difficulty speaking…? Patient: No, I can speak fine.” and “any visual problems…? Patient: I, I don't think so, but I wear glasses.”
Systemic symptoms described: “I generally feel tired, and weak. And, sometimes I feel nauseous, and I don't feel like I want to do anything.”
No past medical history reported: “Do you have any other illnesses at all? Patient: No.”

Medication and dose: “I take an aspirin, seventy five milligrams, once a day, but that's, because of something I read on the internet.” and started after father’s operation: “I started… taking it after my, father had his operation.”
Allergy explicitly stated: “Do you, have any, um, allergies…? Patient: I'm allergic to penicillin only.”
Father’s carotid surgery: “my, father has had a, operation to the side of his neck, to reduce the risk of stroke,” which corresponds to carotid surgery to reduce stroke risk.
Social history: “I'm, uh, I'm actually a doctor… I work in, uh, plastic surgery.” and “No, I live with my wife.” and “Do you smoke at all? Patient: No, I don't.”

Recurrent unilateral deficits over 1.5–2 months with increasing frequency are described, and GP concern for TIA: onset and frequency as above, plus “they make me concerned about, mini-strokes or TIAs, transient ischemic attacks.”

Self-initiated aspirin and no prior GP counseling: “I take an aspirin… because of something I read on the internet” and “that wasn't the doctor telling me” and “has any GP ever spoken to you about, the risks of Aspirin…? Patient: No, I haven't.”
Family cerebrovascular disease implied: “father has had a, operation to the side of his neck, to reduce the risk of stroke,” which is a cerebrovascular risk procedure.

Urgent TIA clinic referral and timing: “I'm going to, refer you to a stroke, a TIA clinic… they'll usually, call you in within the next one to two days” and “that's the kind of turnaround we're, we're looking at.”

Planned workup: “they'll be doing a ultrasound of the, carotid arteries… and, they'll be doing a, maybe a, they might do a scan of your brain as well.” This corresponds to carotid Doppler and brain imaging as indicated.
ED precautions: “If your symptoms return and they persist, they're prolonged. Then um, you may need to attend A and E… we want you to go to hospital in that instance, as soon as possible.”

Contact details and advice to call: “The hospital, you can actually ring them, on… the PALS number, and then there's also the TIA clinic number. I'm going to leave that number in the notes… if you want, you can ring them, either today or tomorrow morning… just to find out when they got time to slot you in… and they're going to be calling you in.”

Safety net re delays/attendance: “if there's any delay that, transpires for example, you can't make the appointment or, you know, they, you don't get called. you, you get, get in contact back, back with us, OK.”
